s: a roaster's café in the Hühnermarkt, the old town's former chicken-market square
w: Set in the Hühnermarkt -- the square that took its name from Frankfurt's old chicken market -- this café from local roaster Hoppenworth & Ploch opened in 2019 as part of the rebuilt old town. Sustainably sourced coffee and good pastries in a small, calm room among the reconstructed timber-frame houses, drawing locals rather than the Römer crowds a few streets over.
_facts: Located at Markt 22, 60311 Frankfurt am Main, in the Hühnermarkt square of the rebuilt Altstadt
Opened in 2019 by Frankfurt roaster Hoppenworth & Ploch
Hühnermarkt ("chicken market") is named for the square's historic market function
Part of Frankfurt's reconstructed Altstadt (Dom-Römer) quarter, completed 2018

s: a family-run multi-roaster specialty café on the old town's gallery street
w: A family-owned specialty coffee shop on Fahrgasse, the gallery-lined street on the edge of the old town, pouring precise espresso, flat whites and V60 since December 2015. Industrial-leaning decor and serious bean sourcing have made it a name coffee people travel across the city for, tucked among the art dealers rather than the postcard corner of the Altstadt.
_facts: Located at Fahrgasse 7, 60311 Frankfurt am Main
Family-owned specialty coffee shop, open since December 2015
Fahrgasse is known locally as a street of art galleries at the edge of the old town
Sells its own roasted beans alongside espresso, flat white, cappuccino and V60

s: the covered market hall Frankfurters fought to save and rebuilt after the war
w: A clinker-brick covered market a block off the Zeil shopping street, destroyed in the war and rebuilt after locals pushed back against plans to scrap it entirely. Dozens of stalls sell regional produce, cheese, bread, cured meats and hot food across two levels, with counters where you eat standing rather than just shop -- a genuinely used, everyday market rather than a tourist food court.
_facts: Located at Hasengasse 5-7, 60311 Frankfurt am Main, near the Zeil shopping street
Market hall damaged in WWII and rebuilt; saved from redevelopment by local public pressure
Around 60 stalls selling regional produce, cheese, meat, bread and prepared food
Includes eat-in counters and a gallery level

s: an owner-built neighbourhood café in the heart of Apfelwein Sachsenhausen
w: A small, carefully built café on Große Rittergasse in Sachsenhausen, opened in August 2018 by owner Sven with visible attention to detail throughout. Quality coffee and homemade food draw a steady neighbourhood crowd in an area better known for its Apfelwein taverns -- a quiet daytime counterpoint a short walk from the river.
_facts: Located at Große Rittergasse 20, 60594 Frankfurt am Main, Sachsenhausen-Nord
Opened 12 August 2018, built out personally by owner Sven
Known for specialty coffee and homemade food in a small, calm space
Sachsenhausen is Frankfurt's traditional Apfelwein (cider) tavern district
